plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and lag uncertainty to calibrate later steps and hold-input estimate for target control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y should rise steadily from ~0.22 toward ~0.4-0.6 with a few seconds lag and visible noise ripple.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and dead-zone uncertainty by testing max amplitude versus E1 0.5 level to determine what input can lift level toward target.
experiments.expected_observation: If high-input gain with dead-zone above ~0.5 is correct, y should stop decaying and rise within 2-4 s toward ~0.25-0.35 with visible pump effect; if y keeps decaying like E1, max pump authority is very low.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures u=0 drain decay rate and time constant, needed to estimate feedforward hold input and integrator requirement for target control.
experiments.expected_observation: If drain with lag is correct, y should decay gradually from ~0.30 toward ~0.18-0.22 over 10-12 s, not instantly, with ~0.01 noise ripple; if y stays flat, drain is negligible.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces intermediate-gain and linearity uncertainty between u=0.5 sink and u=1.0 rise to estimate hold input needed for y=0.6 control.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain is positive with 1-2 s lag, y should stay flat ~0.20 for 1-2 s then rise toward ~0.30-0.38 over 10 s with +/-0.015 noise; if y stays flat or keeps decaying, dead-zone/threshold extends to 0.8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces intermediate-gain and linearity uncertainty between u=0.5 sink and u=1.0 rise to locate threshold and estimate hold input for y=0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with 2-4 s lag is correct, y should hold near 0.20 for 1-2 s then rise toward ~0.28-0.32 at ~0.01-0.02/s with +/-0.015 noise; if dead-zone extends to 0.75, y will stay flat or decay like E1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces intermediate-gain and linearity uncertainty between u=0.75 flat and u=1.0 rise to locate threshold and estimate hold input for y=0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with 2-4 s lag is correct, y should stay near 0.18-0.21 for 2-4 s then rise toward ~0.25-0.30 at ~0.01/s with +/-0.015 noise; if dead-zone extends to 0.8, y will stay flat or decay like E1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces high-level gain and linearity uncertainty to estimate hold input needed for y=0.6 control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain persists at higher level, y should rise from ~0.33 toward ~0.42-0.45 at ~0.015-0.025/s with +/-0.015 noise and 1-2 s lag; if drain grows fast with level or inflow saturates, rise will flatten below ~0.40.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces high-level gain and hold-input uncertainty for y=0.6, which determines feedforward and whether target is reachable below saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain persists at higher level, y should rise from ~0.46 toward ~0.54-0.57 at ~0.02-0.025/s after 1-2 s lag with +/-0.015 noise; if drain grows strongly with level, rise will flatten below ~0.52.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces steady-state hold-input and high-level gain uncertainty for y=0.6, which sets feedforward and whether target is reachable below saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold for y=0.6 needs ~0.85-0.95, y should stay near 0.58-0.62 or decay slightly at ~-0.005 to -0.015/s after 1-2 s lag with +/-0.015 noise; if hold is much lower, y will keep rising like E8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces steady-state hold-input and high-level gain uncertainty for y=0.6, which sets feedforward and determines whether target is reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold for y=0.6 is ~0.65-0.75, y should flatten after 1-2 s lag then hold near 0.62-0.66 or decay slightly at -0.005 to -0.02/s with +/-0.015 noise; if hold is <=0.6, y will keep rising like E9 toward ~0.68.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures high-level drain rate at u=0 from ~0.70 to resolve hold-input vs lag confusion from short E9/E10 and to size feedforward/integrator for y=0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If lag 1-3 s plus drain ~0.015-0.02/s is correct, y should hold near 0.69-0.71 for 1-2 s then decay toward ~0.53-0.60 over 10 s with +/-0.015 noise; if y keeps rising, prior E9/E10 rises were not lag carryover.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces steady-state hold-input uncertainty for y=0.6 by testing u=0.55 from below, discriminating hold ~0.5 versus ~0.6 to set feedforward for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold for y=0.6 is ~0.5-0.6 with 2-4 s lag, y should stay near 0.47 for 1-2 s then rise toward ~0.50-0.55 at ~0.01-0.02/s with +/-0.015 noise; if hold is >0.6, y will stay flat or decay.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases y with positive steady-state gain.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
There is no large dead-zone; u=0.5 produces a clear rise above drain and noise.
Response has lag/time-constant of a few seconds, not instantaneous.
Steady-state input to hold y=0.6 is in [0.3, 0.7].
Response is approximately linear across input levels.
Sensor noise standard deviation is small, <0.02.
